penalties_applied.name: not_legitimate_or_grey
penalties_applied.reason: Any product that attempts to strip or circumvent ads on Meta/Instagram/Facebook platforms would violate Meta's Terms of Service and potentially the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (automated scraping/modification of platform content). A browser-extension ad-blocker for social platforms sits in a persistent legal and TOS grey zone. Adjacent plays (curated newsletters, feed managers) do not — but those are different, weaker opportunities not described in this candidate.

rationale: The underlying signal — that some users would pay to avoid social-media ads — is real, but there is no buildable product here for a solo operator. The buyer is a vague 'high-income professional' with no specific role, budget line, or reachability path; willingness to pay is expressed as a hypothetical ($170/yr for a platform feature the platform won't offer), not as spend on a substitute. Any direct implementation (ad-stripping browser tool, automated feed cleaner on Meta) violates platform TOS and carries legal exposure, triggering the not_legitimate_or_grey penalty. Adjacent ideas (ad-free newsletters, curated content digests) are genuinely different opportunities that would need to be scoped separately — they are not what this candidate describes.
solution_plan: There is no viable product to build from this signal as stated. The structural barrier — Meta's TOS and economic incentives — is not something a solo operator can engineer around legitimately. If Youval wants to explore the adjacent space (e.g. a curated, ad-free weekly digest of niche professional content delivered by email), that should be filed as a new, separate opportunity with a defined ICP and monetisation model. This candidate should be dropped.
notes: not_legitimate_or_grey penalty applied: any direct ad-suppression tool on Meta/Instagram violates platform TOS. Scored 0.0 after penalty. Drop.
